body.statement: Fix \(\mathcal A\). If the directed part of \(H\) is acyclic and has no directed self-loop, let \(G^\star\) contain every permitted directed lag and bidirected offset. The ancestors of \(\{X_{-\gamma},Y_0\}\) in \(G^\star\) lie in \(V\times[-\gamma-(n-1)L,0]\), contain at most \(n(nL+1)\) vertices, and one ordinary ID call on this ancestral ADMG is sound and complete for uniform identification over \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), with every returned probability evaluated on the common product alphabet.
body.justification: The proposition supplies a nontrivial solved subclass and a required reduction test for the general transducer.
body.gap: Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui use a densest candidate full-time graph to validate adjustment under causal sufficiency, and Jahn--Karnik--Schulman analyze one fully specified periodic latent-confounded graph. This reduction instead uses one saturated ancestral ADMG to decide general fixing-based identification uniformly over unknown lag refinements and supplies exact-summary stationary negative witnesses.
body.consumer: Acyclic EasyRCA summaries can be screened immediately with an ordinary finite ID implementation.

obligation.what_is_open: The completeness direction: turning ordinary-ID failure on the saturated ancestral ADMG into two models in the fixed class \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) with the same entire stationary law.
obligation.obstruction: An ordinary finite-ADMG hedge can contain several time roles of one coordinate. The advertised independent-shift construction stores those roles as coordinate slots, changing \(\mathcal A_i\) to a product alphabet. Exact-summary padding adds further slots. Therefore the current negative lift does not land in the fixed-alphabet class quantified by this proposition.
obligation.attempted: I verified the ancestor bound and supergraph soundness, then audited the negative shift construction at the coordinate, intervention, and outcome-event types. The mismatch occurs before any hedge arithmetic and cannot be repaired by relabeling when, for example, \(|\mathcal A_i|=2\) but two binary slots are required.
obligation.partial_result: The ancestor bound and the soundness half are proved in \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}id\text{-}soundness}\): a successful ordinary ID call on at most \(n(nL+1)\) vertices returns one uniform finite-cylinder functional.  What remains unproved is the converse implication from failure of ID on \(G^\star[A^\star]\) to two strictly stationary countermodels on the fixed alphabet family \(\mathcal A\).
